Subject: Deployment mode follow-up & region/routing clarifications — Nova AI

Hi Olivia / Simon — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on the right deployment mode for your platform: 

Recap (short):
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer-facing inference and audit logs; secondary requirement to support APAC traffic with low latency later this year.
- Compliance: SOC2 and DPA required; some customers may request contractual language for controlled unencrypted telemetry.
- Preference: You are evaluating Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved EU pool), and Private (VPC / on-prem) for full control.

Key questions for qualification:
1) Which workloads must NEVER leave EU (inference + logs vs just inference)? Please list any countries that require on-prem (if any).
2) Expected steady-state TPS and peak QPS (requests/s) and typical sequence lengths/response token sizes.
3) Latency targets (p90/p99) for EU and APAC users.
4) Any specific vendor constraints (allowed cloud regions or on-prem restrictions)?

High-level options and trade-offs (so we’re aligned):
- Hosted (EU region): Fastest to get started; we can pin the Hosted API to EU regions for data-in-residence, but for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools in an EU region (SLA, capacity isolation). Good trade-off if you want predictable throughput and contractual residency assurances. Provisioning ~4–6 weeks depending on capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full network isolation and control over KMS/HSM. Best for regulated customers who need on-prem or strict network controls. Onboarding timeline and ops footprint higher (varies by customer infra).

Attachments: SOC2 summary + a short deployment-options one-pager attached.

Suggested next steps:
- Olivia, can you confirm the answers to Q1–Q3 above?
- If feasible, let’s schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45 min) with your infra team to review routing, latency expectations, and a sample traffic profile. I’ve proposed some times in a follow-up.

Thanks —

Thanks for the clear notes, Dylan — adding technical clarifications so we can set expectations correctly on residency & routing: 

Short answers up front:
- Hosted EU region: Supported. We offer Hosted endpoints operating in EU zones and can keep inference compute and short-term KV/prefix caches in-region.
- Cross-region routing: By default, our smart routing sends requests to the nearest healthy region; for strict residency requirements we can enforce region pinning or route-by-policy, but true tenant isolation requires Dedicated or Private.
- Logs & metrics: For Hosted, aggregate metrics and traces are replicated to our control plane (US by default) unless Enterprise DPA controls are in place; we can configure log forwarding and region-local retention for enterprise customers.

Longer detail / trade-offs:
- Hosted (EU pinned): Fastest path; supports EU compute and-per-route region preference. However, control plane metadata and some audit trails may remain in our managed plane unless we enable the Enterprise residency add-on (requires DPA + account scoping). Good for early proof-of-concept or low-regulated workloads.
- Dedicated (EU reserved pool): Compute plus ephemeral caches and customer routing live in the reserved EU pool. We can sign tighter contractual residency guarantees and set retention windows for logs inside the region. Provisioning timeline: 4–6 weeks after PO and infra allocation; engineering lead time 1–2 weeks for capacity planning.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full data plane control. We ship a private control plane option (customer-managed networking) and offer an on-prem appliance for customers that must keep data isolated. Onboarding is variable — typically 6–12 weeks depending on network & security review.

APAC notes:
- We have APAC regions but capacity availability depends on reserved pools. If Nova needs low-latency APAC support at GA, consider Dedicated with burst/cross-region configuration or plan for a Private deployment in APAC later. Typical APAC enablement for Dedicated is 8–12 weeks.

Ask from us to accelerate qualification:
- Minimal traffic profile (steady QPS, peak QPS), token distribution (avg output tokens), and a sample latency SLO (p99 target).
- Data sensitivity classification (PII, Health, Financial) to pick correct onboarding path.

I’ll prep a short architecture diagram and a matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private by next-day.

— Dev
